text: Don Matías is a municipality located in the Northern Antioquia subregion of the Antioquia Department, Colombia. It is bordered to the north by Santa Rosa de Osos, to the east by Santa Rosa de Osos and Santo Domingo, to the south by Barbosa, and to the west by San Pedro de los Milagros. Since 1624, the area has been inhabited by settlers from Santa Fe de Antioquia; starting in 1750, the settlements of San Andrés, Las Ánimas, Las Juntas, and La Chorrera were populated and now form the urban population. This settlement pattern resulted from policies implemented by the Bourbon crown, specifically through the efforts of the visitor Mon y Velarde in Antioquia, aimed at establishing agricultural colonies in the northern part of the province. The early inhabitants were primarily mazamorreros, independent miners, who were granted titles for their plots. The municipality has had three names: Azuero, San Antonio Infante, and Don Matías, the latter being adopted in 1787 in honor of Don Matías Jaramillo, who had a significant mining settlement in the area. In the 1960s, the garment industry was established in Don Matías due to the decentralization of manufacturing industries in Medellín, leading to the arrival of an industrial clothing company that mainly produced for Caribou. This provided employment, as the municipality was previously predominantly agrarian. A decade later, former workers began setting up their own small garment factories. Today, Don Matías enjoys extensive national and international recognition, with the Riogrande Dam being one of its main attractions. The 2018 census recorded a population of 14,208; in 2009, the total population was 19,458, with 12,663 urban and 6,795 rural inhabitants. The literacy rate was 91.3% in 2005. According to the Government of Antioquia’s Quality of Life survey from 2004, 70.9% of homes are in socio-economic stratum 2 (low), followed by 23.3% in stratum 3 (medium-low), 4.4% in stratum 1 (low-high), and 1.4% in stratum 4 (medium). The DANE census of 2005 indicates the ethnic-racial composition of the municipality. Don Matías’ economy is primarily based on the textile and apparel industry, pig farming, dairy cattle, and the timber industry. Its geographic coordinates are 6°29′N 75°26′W (6.483°N 75.433°W).
